gaps.why_now: Phase 11 now has multiple bounded starters that touch watchdog and hvc surfaces, so one shared note keeps the public-header boundary explicit instead of leaving reviewers to infer that UAPI and shared core ownership still remain outside the tranche.

A dedicated shared survey gate now verifies that the Phase 11 note, the watchdog headers, the hvc header, and the driver-local survey packets all still describe the same bounded public-header posture.

The dw_wdt lane now records that include/uapi/linux/watchdog.h still owns struct watchdog_info plus the WDIOC_* and WDIOF_* or WDIOS_* surface, while include/linux/watchdog.h still owns watchdog_device and watchdog_ops so the DesignWare starter does not overclaim watchdog parity.

The hvc_console starter already carries a tiny header-parity snapshot for drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_console.h that mirrors MAX_NR_HVC_CONSOLES, HVC_ALLOC_TTY_ADAPTERS, the hv_ops callback shape, and exported hvc helper metadata without widening into tty registration or host-backed I/O.

The shared header-parity gate now carries one bounded layout_assert checkpoint for struct watchdog_info so size, alignment, and field offsets stay reviewable without turning this simple-driver slice into a wider watchdog-core ownership claim.

The shared header-parity gate now carries one bounded layout_assert checkpoint for struct winsize so the hvc resize surface keeps size, alignment, and ws_row/ws_col/ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel offsets reviewable without claiming tty-core or struct hvc_struct ownership.

If a later Phase 11 driver begins mirroring public-header constants or shared struct layouts beyond these bounded snapshots, the honest next step is a driver-local checkpoint plus an explicit handoff to the Phase 3 interop substrate rather than a silent simple-driver parity claim.
